title: The Copper Orchard
premise: In 1847, in the river town of Copperbridge, Wren Eastwick inherits the unfinished atlas of their dead master, Halvard, whose final map charts something no one commissioned: a hidden ledger of debts, bribes, and a massacre at the copper orchard that the victorious mining company has spent a decade erasing. When the seasonal bridge closes and the company's hired historians arrive to 'settle' the record before spring, Wren — sheltered by an orchard of survivors who have become an unlikely family — must finish Halvard's atlas as testimony rather than art. Racing floods, fire, and betrayal from within, Wren gets the truth engraved, printed, and into the hands of a distant magistrate just as the ice breaks; justice arrives late and imperfect, but the record stands, and Wren finally understands that history happens to everyone, everywhere.
about_author: Odile Nystrom is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing suppressed regional maps before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted ferry house on a cold northern river, where she keeps a wall of unfinished atlases by authors who never got credit.

chapters.title: The Last Commission
chapters.summary: Wren Eastwick, POV. Inking the final plate of Master Halvard's atlas, Wren finds a sealed folio hidden beneath the drafting table — maps of places Halvard never visited, dated after his death. The beat: quiet dread beneath routine grief.

chapters.title: Bridge Out
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The company announces the bridge closes for winter repairs; the last ferry leaves at dusk. Wren chooses to stay and finish the atlas, watching the far shore — and the company's surveyors — recede. Beat: the trap closing gently.

chapters.title: The Orchard People
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Seeking lodging, Wren is taken in by the residents of the derelict copper orchard: Maren the herbalist, old Piet, and twins Sef and Ilse. They knew Halvard. Beat: wary hospitality becoming warmth.

chapters.title: What Halvard Drew
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She reveals the orchard was once a company village, cleared violently in 1837; Halvard mapped it afterward, collecting testimony. The folio is evidence. Beat: grief recontextualized as inheritance.

chapters.title: Guests Across the River
chapters.summary: Company historian Ambrose Vell's POV. Vell arrives to write the official centenary history, confident and charming, tasked with burying the orchard file permanently. Beat: elegant menace.

chapters.title: The Ledger Plate
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Deciphering Halvard's coded marginalia, Wren finds names, dates, and payments matching the massacre night. First attempt to copy the plate nearly exposes them. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Sef's River
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. A smuggler's run across the half-frozen river to test whether word can reach the outside; he returns chased, having lost the sample letter but confirmed the crossing is possible — barely. Beat: hope with a cost.

chapters.title: Vell Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vell visits under pretense of buying Halvard's papers, offering money and flattery. Wren lies well for the first time in their life. Beat: the apprentice outgrowing obedience.

chapters.title: Ilse's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She was a child in 1837 and finally speaks the whole night aloud while Wren records it verbatim. The room holds her like a net. Beat: catharsis; the atlas becomes a witness.

chapters.title: A Traitor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Piet's POV. Piet, terrified for the young ones, secretly contacts Vell offering the folio in exchange for amnesty. He tells himself it is protection. Beat: love curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: Fire in the Map Room
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Halvard's town workshop burns; the original plates survive only because Wren had moved them. Suspicion falls on drifters; Wren knows better. Beat: escalation, first bloodless casualty.

chapters.title: The Frozen Crossing
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren leads the full testimony packet toward the crossing; the ice cracks; Piet confesses his bargain mid-river and turns back to mislead Vell instead. Beat: redemption purchased with exposure.

chapters.title: House Search
chapters.summary: Vell's POV. Company men ransack the orchard legally, warrant in hand. Wren has split the evidence — half engraved onto innocent-looking decorative plates. Vell suspects but cannot prove. Beat: cat-and-mouse intimacy of enemies.

chapters.title: Engraving by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A montage chapter: the found family becomes a print shop, each person given a task, Wren teaching and being taught. Beat: found family crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Magistrate Owes
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. A letter surfaces showing the magistrate himself took orchard money years ago; their chosen destination is compromised. Despair — then Sef proposes a newspaper editor two towns over. Beat: plan B born of desperation.

chapters.title: Vell's Offer
chapters.summary: Vell's POV. Genuinely moved by Ilse's recorded voice, Vell offers Wren a deal: print the truth softened, names withheld, and no one is prosecuted for obstruction. Wren refuses. Beat: the antagonist's humanity without absolution.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Piet
chapters.summary: Piet's POV. Vell, feeling betrayed, has Piet detained as the arsonist. The family debates rescue versus the mission. Beat: duty to one against duty to all — the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The river begins breaking up early; the bridge reopens in days and Vell will leave with the confiscated 'official' plates. Everything must move tonight. Beat: clock running loud.

chapters.title: The Night Run
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The climax: a diversionary fire at the tollhouse frees Piet while Maren and Wren run the proof sheets across the rotting ice as it fails beneath them. Wren nearly drowns saving the last plate. Beat: terror, sacrifice, triumph.

chapters.title: Ink on the Record
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The editor prints the atlas excerpts and testimonies under banner headlines; copies ride the morning coach to the capital before Vell's version ships. Beat: exhale — truth outrunning power by hours.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Men
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Spring brings investigators, arrests of company officers, and also summons for the orchard folk. Justice is slow, partial, real. Vell departs unbowed but diminished. Beat: bittersweet vindication.

chapters.title: The Open Atlas
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With the bridge open and the world suddenly reachable, Wren chooses to stay through one full growing season, finishing the atlas properly with every name included, then packs Halvard's folio for the road. Beat: home as a choice, not a cage.
